| [CLAIM-581](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-581.md) v3 | Under peak-capacity costs on reversible moves, the transition threshold between configurations is an extended pseudo-ultrametric, so identifying configurations reachable within a budget is an equivalence relation at every budget and the identifications nest into one tree as the budget grows; under additive costs the threshold is only an extended pseudometric, budgeted identification need not be transitive, and no such tree exists | The assistant's own proposition, filed on 2026-11-05 at the owner's invitation to contribute. Take configurations joined by reversible moves, each move with a peak requirement, and let d(x, y) be the least, over paths, of the largest requirement on the path ([CLAIM-571](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-571.md)'s threshold, identities free). Concatenating a path from x to y with one from y to z has peak max(d(x, y), d(y, z)), so d(x, z) ≤ max(d(x, y), d(y, z)): d is an extended pseudo-ultrametric (distinct states joined at no cost are at distance 0, unjoined ones at ∞; it is an ultrametric only when every pair of distinct states is separated by a positive cost). Hence at each budget b, "x and y can be turned into one another within b" is an equivalence relation, its classes are the components of the budget-b move graph, and as b grows the classes only merge, forming one dendrogram, the merge tree of zero-dimensional sublevel persistence (Mirth et al.). Under additive costs d is a metric and budgeted identification is intransitive in general. So which resource semantics governs a system decides whether "the same thing, within budget" sorts its configurations into a hierarchy of kinds at all. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |

| [CLAIM-597](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-597.md) v2 | Where every replacement part is supplied from outside, an organization can become independent of what founded it but never of what feeds it: with damage at rate d and supplied repair at rate ρs the intact fraction holds at ρs/(ρs + d), needs a supply growing as θ/(1 − θ) times the damage rate to hold a share θ, and decays as e^(−dt) once the supply stops, as DNA origami that self-heals from a strand pool and origami that replicates from supplied monomers both illustrate | The assistant's, on the owner's invitation of 2026-11-05 to add readings and claims to the DNA origami filing. | [CLAIM-600](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-600.md) v2 | Transient support can be withdrawn safely when it starts a process that keeps itself going on a flux that will stay available, when it is large enough to carry the supported party past any threshold that process has, when the threat it stood in for has gone, and when the party could do the work and did it throughout; inputs the party cannot produce must stay supplied as a standing part of the arrangement, support that fails these leaves dependence or decay, and persistence after withdrawal is needed to tell which, though slow reversion can mimic it | The assistant's, at the owner's request of 2026-11-05 to characterize "what differentiates transient support that induces dependency and is hazardous to remove from transient support that builds new capabilities and is safe to remove", with reintroduction and ecological recovery proposed as cases. It draws together the branch's three domains: DNA origami, aid and development, and ecology. Three conditions decide it. First, the support starts a self-sustaining process on an ambient flux instead of doing the upkeep. Planted tree islands, weeded for 2.5 years, kept their advantage to 16–18 years because established trees keep drawing seed dispersers (Holl et al.; Schubert et al.). Supplied repair, by contrast, never becomes optional ([CLAIM-597](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-597.md)). Second, the threat it stood in for is gone. Conservation-reliant species stay reliant while fire is suppressed or habitat threats persist (Mussmann et al.; Brown et al.). Third, the party did the work throughout. Support that does the work wears capacity down by disuse ([CLAIM-558](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-558.md)), by slack effort (Ostrom et al.) or by selection for the supported conditions, which costs hatchery steelhead fitness in the wild within one generation (Christie et al.). Captive-bred translocated stock shows negative population growth (Morris et al.). Persistence must be shown after withdrawal: impact at exit and judged success both overstate it. Revised the same day after two counterpoints the owner asked for. Evidence against the lazy-poor stereotype finds no slack effort in poor households: cash transfers barely change work, and one-off graduation packages raise it. So that route is confined to help that is assured and permanent. A household asset threshold (Balboni et al.) adds a condition on size: support too small decays with no dependence at all. Urban development adds three cautions. Some public inputs are a standing part of a coproduced service (Evans; Watson). Forty years of persistence can be slow reversion (Kline and Moretti). And a place can last while the people it served are dispersed (Collins and Shester; LaVoice). The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-601](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-601.md) v2 | A savings buffer is a stock of time: where shocks must be absorbed or a household is ruined, an investment that pays only after a delay is worth taking only above a buffer that rises with the delay, so households with the same preferences decline profitable delayed investments below it, a choice that reads as impatience and is the right policy for survival by a deadline; covering needs through the delay buys the time | The assistant's, after the owner read Haushofer and Fehr's finding, that deprivation produces short-sighted choices, as decision-making under a resource constraint: "deprivation induces added time pressure to the decision making process." A toy shows the consequence. Savings move +1 or −1 each period, and the household can pay 3 now for 6 later. Investing raises survival over 40 periods only above a buffer of 4 when the payoff comes after 1 period, rising to 5, 6, 9 and 14 at delays of 4, 9, 16 and 25. Below it, declining is right. Survival, the objective deprivation makes binding, needs a deeper buffer than expected wealth. At delay 16 and buffer 8, investing raises expected wealth from 8.15 to 10.30 and lowers survival from 0.846 to 0.835. Covering shocks through the delay lowers the threshold to the outlay alone, which is what graduation programmes' consumption support does. The time pressure here is the planning horizon. Deliberation time and attention are a second sense, left to the scarcity readings. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |
| [CLAIM-602](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md) v2 | Where an organization's capacity is learned by doing the work it serves, and decays with disuse, outside supply that does the work first lowers the capacity kept, and the longer it does all of it the longer recovery takes once it stops, while supply that covers only what the organization cannot yet do leaves its learning untouched, so what decides dependence is the order in which supply and capacity are used, not the amount of supply | The assistant's, at the owner's request of 2026-11-05 to look to aid and development for theory on how aid-dependent organizations become self-sufficient. In a model where capacity grows with the work done and decays with disuse ([CLAIM-558](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-558.md)), aid that does a share A of the work first holds capacity at λ(1 − A)/(λ(1 − A) + μ): with λ = 1, μ = 0.3, 0.769 without aid, 0.625 at A = 0.5, 0.25 at 0.9 and none at full substitution. After full substitution for 10, 20 and 40 time units, meeting demand takes 3.8, 6.4 and 11.4 units once aid stops, because the work an organization can do is capped by its capacity, so it regrows from a seed. The first point is Azam et al.'s; the second and third are not in their paper. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |
| [CLAIM-603](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-603.md) | A capability lost because another reliably supplies it is the Black Queen's loss, favoured to the one who loses it, and whether it is dependency or division of labour is decided by the supply, not the loss: one-way supply set from outside, as aid is, leaves a dependence that nothing in the dependent's dynamics limits and that withdrawal punishes, while reciprocal loss, each partner supplying what the other gave up, leaves interdependence, so the aim framed as self-sufficiency is better framed as reciprocity | The assistant's, on the owner's remark of 2026-11-05 that "assured help makes recipients lose skill" sounds "closely related to niche differentiation and specialization phenomena". The record holds the biology. On the Black Queen Hypothesis ([THEORY-1048](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1048.md)) a cell that stops making a leaky public good saves its cost while others still supply it, so the loss is favoured to the individual and spreads. Buchnera ([THEORY-1103](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1103.md)) has lost the genes its host covers and kept those its host lacks. The Samaritan's dilemma has the same logic (Ostrom et al.), and Azam, Devarajan and O'Connell's recipient is better off in the high-aid state. The loss itself is not the pathology. What differs is the supply. A Black Queen loss stops by itself when helpers grow rare, because the helpers are the same population. Aid is set from outside and does not fall as dependence grows, so nothing stops the loss short of what aid covers, and withdrawal returns the cost ([CLAIM-602](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md)). Buchnera's loss runs both ways, and the result is interdependence. A state that taxes its citizens (Moore) is in the same position: it lost nothing, it exchanges. After the owner linked the claim to the gift economy of Burning Man, readings of Mauss, of St John on Burning Man and of Heins, Unrau and Avram added two things. One-way supply costs the receiver standing as well as capacity: in Mauss the unreturned gift makes its receiver inferior. And the return need not go back to the giver: it can travel round a circuit, as Mauss's do, or out to a whole community, as Burning Man's is meant to, and both sit beside a demand for self-reliance. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-604](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-604.md) v2 | Where each damaged part of a structure is repaired by drawing on a flux at a rate proportional to the structure's intact share, as a flame's upkeep is, it has an ignition threshold below which it goes out with the supply still on, a supply level below which it collapses rather than declines, and an outage after which restoring the supply does not relight it; repair supplied at a rate set by the supply alone, whatever the structure's state, has none of the three | The assistant's, at the owner's request of 2026-11-05 to connect [CLAIM-597](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-597.md)'s supplied maintenance to the record's dissipative structures. The record separates order held by an outside flow, the Bénard cell, from order that keeps up the conditions of its own maintenance, the candle flame ([THEORY-072](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-072.md), [TERM-070](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-070.md), [QUESTION-085](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-085.md)). [CLAIM-597](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-597.md) modelled only the first. The second is modelled by letting uptake from the flux scale with the intact share: dI/dt = −dI + κsI²(1 − I). With d = 0.2 and κs = 2 the structure holds 0.887, as supplied repair at ρs = 1.575 does, but it goes out from 0.10 with the supply on, collapses when the supply falls below 40 % of its level, and after an outage longer than about 10.3 time units does not relight when the supply returns. Supplied repair recovers from any start and declines smoothly. Both decay as e^(−dt) once the supply stops, so the self-maintaining structure is no less dependent on the flux. What it gains is independence from a provider who delivers repair, at the price of thresholds. That gives [QUESTION-085](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-085.md) three observable signatures. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |
| [CLAIM-605](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-605.md) v2 | Where capacity is learned by doing, decays with disuse and needs capacity already present to grow, support that does the work has a deadline after which withdrawal no longer restores capacity, and a slow taper of such support is worse than an abrupt cut because it holds practice down long enough to cross the threshold; support that covers only what the party cannot yet do needs no taper but cannot lift a party already below the threshold | The assistant's, filling gaps the supplied-maintenance filing left, at the owner's request of 2026-11-05 to "proceed systematically filling all of those identified gaps". [CLAIM-602](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md) modelled crowding out with no threshold, so capacity always regrew from a seed. Its own limits named the threshold case, Azam et al.'s trap. The model gives three results. Support that does all the work has a deadline: after ln(0.7/0.276)/0.3 = 3.10 time units capacity has crossed the threshold, and withdrawal no longer restores it. Capacity-first support needs no taper, since it withdraws itself, but it cannot lift a party already below the threshold. | [CLAIM-606](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-606.md) v2 | A localized structure can persist by an internal balance that needs no supply, by a balance of gain and loss that needs a standing supply, or by a topological charge that continuous change cannot remove, and the three differ in what carries the structure's identity, how it forms and how it ends; because thresholds and abrupt ends appear in all of them, even with no supply at all, only withdrawing the supply and measuring the outflow tells which route a structure is on | The assistant's, after the owner's hunch that "the physics/dynamics of soliton formation could be a valuable angle through which to consider some of our questions about individuation and persistence". Solitons give three routes by which a localized structure persists. - Integrable solitons are held by an internal balance and need no
  supply. They come in a family set by their initial data, and they keep
  their identity through collisions.
- Dissipative solitons are held by a supplied balance of gain and loss.
  Their shape is "predetermined by the equation parameters, rather than
  by the initial conditions", and they last "until the pump laser is
  switched off".
- Topological solitons carry a charge that continuous change cannot
  remove.
A fourth case, the oscillon, has none of the three protections. It forms only from a window of initial sizes, settles to a common state regardless of where it started, holds for a thousand oscillations, and then ends abruptly. That bears on two of the record's claims. - It qualifies [CLAIM-604](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-604.md). Thresholds and abrupt ends appear with no
  supply at all, and in Kerr solitons with a supply that does not depend

- It sharpens [CLAIM-600](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-600.md). Persistence through many turnovers is not

The routes are told apart by what happens when the supply is withdrawn and by whether an outflow is measured. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
